messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT: P0 - continuous-batcher queue growth -> multiple container crashes in us-east-1 :rotating_light:
oncall-bot: Alert triggered: average queuing time > 2s and GPU memory pressure > 92% across batcher nodes

alex: getting paged, looking now. seeing repeated CUDA OOM logs on batcher-3 and batcher-7
maya: same, nodes are flapping - kube events show CrashLoopBackOff on the runtime container
sre-jordan: quick summary: continuous-batcher backlog grew after a spike of long sequences. KV cache eviction didn't keep up; batch size increased heuristically and memory ballooned -> CUDA OOM -> container restart -> raft handoff thrash -> node flaps

eng-ryan: rolling logs excerpt: ```
E CUDA: cuCtxRestore failed: out of memory
E runtime: failed to allocate KV cache (size=1.2GB)
W continuous-batcher: computed batch_keys=500 -> combined seq_len=4096 -> estimated tokens=2.3M
```

alex: mitigation plan: 1) throttle incoming batcher traffic at proxy (rate-limit per-tenant to 5qps) 2) set BATCHER_MAX_BATCH=128 on runtime config 3) cordon & drain the most noisy nodes and restart runtime pods with new config

maya: I'm applying a cluster-wide env override to reduce max batch size, pushing via deploy-bot now
deploy-bot: deploy queued: config-change (BATCHER_MAX_BATCH=128) -> 6 pods updating

sre-jordan: I'm pausing new canaries and moving critical customers to fallback model-route (smaller model) to reduce memory footprint :white_check_mark:

ops-li: FYI, one enterprise customer (acct: AcmeCorp) reported latency spikes and 502s. Customer-ops reached out; they have a running job that sends long-context prompts every few seconds

customer-ops: Already opened a support bridge with AcmeCorp and suggested temporary routing to smaller model. They want ETA

alex: ETA for config rollout ~2m to reach all pods. After that we expect queue drain and memory pressure drop within 5-8m. If not, we'll force scale down continuous-batcher replicas and add emergency autoscale to isolated pool

eng-ryan: found probable root cause: recent change to prefix coalescing increased how often short requests are merged with long requests, creating pathological merged batches during spikes. Reverting that change in canary seems reasonable
maya: can we do a quick rollback? it affects the coalescer binary in runtime v3.4.2 -> rollback to v3.4.1 on canaries then prod if stable

sre-jordan: agree. I'll coordinate rollback after throttle takes effect. Also enabling extra logging for batch sizes to confirm the hypothesis

ops-li: customer update: AcmeCorp accepts fallback routing for the next 30m. they asked for root cause note and SLA credit if sustained impact

alex: handoff: maya -> taking lead on config change and rollback, i'll stay for postmortem and liaise with infra. If we don't see mem drop by +10m, escalate to infra to power-cycle affected nodes
maya: noted, taking lead. tagging @eng-ryan for rollback steps

eng-ryan: rollback steps: ```1) promote runtime v3.4.1 image to staging 2) smoke test with max batch 128 and sample long prompts 3) rollout 25% canary for 5m 4) if stable, gradual 100% rollout```

oncall-bot: Reminder: create incident page and add customer impact details. Use template /incident create

alex: creating incident page now and adding current timeline + logs

sre-jordan: monitoring: GPU mem usage dropping on batcher-3 after throttle, container restarts reduced. queue length trending down from 1200 -> 280

ops-li: AcmeCorp bridge acknowledges improvement. still seeing occasional 502s for a small subset of long jobs

maya: can we add a temporary prefix cutoff (max_seq_len=2048) at the proxy for public tenants? that'll avoid pathological merges while we rollback

alex: ok applying prefix cutoff to public route. will not apply to enterprise to avoid breaking them - using fallback routing instead

eng-ryan: after rollback + throttle, no further OOMs in last 12m on affected nodes. will keep extra logging for 2h. Next steps: postmortem, rollback PR notes, change to coalescer heuristics to bound merged batch token limit

customer-ops: sent AcmeCorp summary and ETA for postmortem. they requested notification when we close incident

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated - monitoring. Assigning follow-up owners: eng-ryan (root cause + fix), alex (postmortem), maya (rollback verification), sre-jordan (monitoring alerts tuning)

alex: closing on-call shift in 30m, will handoff to next duty. thanks all :thumbsup:
